invariant_set.comparator_hint: C_exists: does a process document exist at the declared CTB position, with all three cluster headers present? Binary.
invariant_set.name: Executable Process
invariant_set.why_it_matters: UP must know this medium exists as a single parseable document with three clusters (Identity/Contract/Governance mapped to Thing/Flow/Change). Without recognizing the medium, UP cannot begin evaluation.

invariant_set.comparator_hint: C_identity: count of 18 required fields (10 process + 8 HEIR) present and non-empty. Ratio: filled/18.
invariant_set.name: Process Identity
invariant_set.why_it_matters: HEIR + ORBT fields are the routing key. An agent cannot filter, prioritize, or check state without identity. A process without identity is unaddressable.

invariant_set.comparator_hint: C_imo: (1) both intake questions answered — binary, (2) Middle table has ≥1 row with all 5 columns filled, (3) Output block names a downstream consumer. Three sub-comparators, all must pass.
invariant_set.name: IMO Declaration
invariant_set.why_it_matters: The Two-Question Intake + Middle step table IS the executable contract. Agents build execution plans from the Middle table rows. Without IMO, the process is a description, not a specification.

invariant_set.comparator_hint: C_osam: (1) READ table has ≥1 row, (2) join chain traces to a declared spine ID, (3) forbidden paths section present (even if empty list). Three sub-comparators.
invariant_set.name: Data Schema
invariant_set.why_it_matters: OSAM tells agents which tables to read, which to write, and the join chain to the spine. Without it, the process touches data blindly — no CQRS enforcement, no join integrity.

invariant_set.comparator_hint: C_dmj: (1) Define table (L19) non-empty, (2) Map table (L20) references all Define element IDs, (3) Join path (L21) reaches spine. Sequential dependency: Step N requires Step N-1 complete.
invariant_set.name: Structure Extraction (DMJ)
invariant_set.why_it_matters: DMJ is the application layer — how raw data becomes structured, mapped, and joined constants. Without it, the process collects data but never structures it. The forced order (Define→Map→Join) is itself a constant.

invariant_set.comparator_hint: C_guardrails: count of declared stop conditions ≥ 6 (the canonical set from Bedrock §6/§8). Missing canonical conditions = unguarded failure modes.
invariant_set.name: Guard Rails
invariant_set.why_it_matters: Stop conditions prevent runaway execution and resource burn. Loaded before execution as halt triggers. Without them, a failing process corrupts data and burns budget.

invariant_set.comparator_hint: C_verify: (1) ≥1 numbered step exists, (2) each step has an expected result, (3) Three Primitives Check present with all three questions. Three sub-comparators.
invariant_set.name: Verification
invariant_set.why_it_matters: The smoke test is the only executable proof the process works. Run FIRST to validate before full pipeline execution. No verification = untestable = undeployable.

invariant_set.comparator_hint: C_measurement: (1) metrics table (L22) has ≥1 metric defined BEFORE build, (2) sigma tracking (L23) active after 3+ runs, (3) ORBT gate rules (L24) present with all four transitions. Three sub-comparators.
invariant_set.name: Measurement
invariant_set.why_it_matters: Analytics define the BUILD→OPERATE gate. Without metrics + sigma tracking + ORBT gate rules, state transitions are subjective. Sigma tracking decides if a process is stable enough to trust.

invariant_set.comparator_hint: C_trace: (1) per-step entry schema declares all 14 required fields, (2) append-only constraint enforced (no UPDATE/DELETE). Two sub-comparators.
invariant_set.name: Execution Trace
invariant_set.why_it_matters: The append-only build journal is what the auditor reads. Without trace entries, certification is impossible. One trace entry must be emitted per Middle table step during execution.

invariant_set.comparator_hint: C_orbt: (1) current ORBT state declared in L5 identity, (2) all four state transitions defined with gate conditions, (3) auditor ≠ builder enforced for BUILD→OPERATE and REPAIR→OPERATE certification gates. Three sub-comparators.
invariant_set.name: ORBT Gate Rules
invariant_set.why_it_matters: The state machine governs process lifecycle. Must check ORBT state before executing — don't run a BUILD-state process as OPERATE. Strike 3 triggers fleet-wide learning via Airworthiness Directive.

layers.format: A named, formatted unit of work that transforms input to output. Self-contained: identity, contract, governance. One document per process. Exists before any execution.
layers.name: Executable Process
layers.zoom_reason: Root medium — must decompose to reveal the three structural clusters mapped to Three Primitives (Thing/Flow/Change). Cannot domesticate: it is the container for all structure below.

layers.format: The set of layers answering WHAT this process IS. Exists before any execution. Three sub-layers: identity (L5), purpose (L6), resources (L7).
layers.name: Identity Cluster
layers.zoom_reason: Structural grouping — three children with distinct schemas (ID fields, prose, resource tables). All children domesticated. Cluster itself is an organizational container used for altitude filtering.

layers.format: The set of layers answering WHAT flows through this process. Five sub-layers: IMO (L8), data schema (L9), structure extraction (L10), C&V output (L11), guard rails (L12).
layers.name: Contract Cluster
layers.zoom_reason: Structural grouping — five children with distinct schemas. All children domesticated. Cluster itself is an organizational container — the executable contract boundary.

layers.format: The set of layers answering HOW this process is controlled, measured, certified, and learned from. Six sub-layers: verification (L13), measurement (L14), execution trace (L15), certification (L16), fleet learning (L17), session history (L18).
layers.name: Governance Cluster
layers.zoom_reason: Structural grouping — six children with distinct governance functions. All children domesticated. Cluster itself is an organizational container for audit and state operations.

layers.format: Two tables: (1) Process table — fields: ID, Name, Medium, Business Silo, CTB Position, ORBT state, Strikes, Authority, Last Modified, Reference. (2) HEIR table — fields: sovereign_ref, hub_id, ctb_placement, imo_topology, cc_layer, services, secrets_provider, acceptance_criteria. 18 total named fields.
layers.name: Process Identity
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — 18 named fields across two fixed tables. All formattable. Decomposing individual fields does not change agent routing or parsing behavior.

layers.format: Prose block: 2-3 sentences. Structural constraint: must name what breaks without this process and what downstream process starves without its output.
layers.name: Purpose
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — single prose block with a fixed constraint (must reference downstream dependency). Content is variable fill. Structure is the constraint, not the prose.

layers.format: Four tables: (1) Dependencies — 4 columns: dependency, type, what it provides, status. (2) Downstream Consumers — 2 columns: consumer, what it needs. (3) Tools & Integrations — 5 columns: item, type, cost tier, credentials, function. (4) Secrets — 4 columns: secret, provider, config, used-by.
layers.name: Resources
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — four table schemas with fixed columns. What fills them varies per process. The structure is domain-agnostic — any process has upstream dependencies, downstream consumers, tools, and secrets.

layers.format: Five sub-components: (1) Two-Question Intake — 2 fixed questions: 'What triggers this?' + 'How do we get it?' (Bedrock §3). (2) Input block — prose. (3) Middle table — 5 columns: Step, Input, What Happens, Output, Tool Used. N rows. (4) Output block — prose + downstream consumer. (5) Circle block — prose feedback loop description (Bedrock §5).
layers.name: IMO Declaration
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — five sub-components with fixed formats. Middle table schema (5 columns) is the constant; step count and content are variable. The same row parser works regardless of step count. Individual steps are domain-variable fill.

layers.format: Four sub-sections: (1) READ table — 3 columns: source, what it provides, join key. (2) WRITE table — 3 columns: target, what it writes, when. (3) Join Chain — tree notation from spine ID. (4) Forbidden Paths — 2 columns: action, why.
layers.name: Data Schema
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — four sub-sections with fixed schemas. Which tables and columns fill them is the variable. Enforces CQRS (Bedrock §4): sub-hubs write, reads go through the join chain. Query routing is derived from the join chain — not a separate structural element.

layers.format: Three ordered steps with forced dependency: Define → Map → Join (DMJ.md). Each step has a distinct table schema (L19, L20, L21). Back-propagation path: Join gaps trigger return to Define (the Circle, Bedrock §5). The order IS the constant. What fills each step is the variable.
layers.name: Structure Extraction (DMJ)
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — all three child layers (L19, L20, L21) are domesticated. The parent's remaining structure is the forced order (Define→Map→Join) + back-propagation rule — both locked by DMJ.md. Agents execute the three steps in sequence using child schemas. No further decomposition changes execution behavior.

layers.format: Two bullet lists: (1) Constants — structure that never changes, bullet items. (2) Variables — fill that changes every run, bullet items. Output of C&V test (Bedrock §2) applied to this specific process.
layers.name: Constants & Variables Declaration
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — two lists with fixed semantics (locked vs guarded). Individual items are variable fill. Used for pre-flight validation — not parsed item-by-item.

layers.format: Table: 2 columns — Condition, Action. Six canonical stop conditions from Bedrock §6 + §8: (1) can't answer Two-Question Intake, (2) data schema gap, (3) 5 consecutive errors, (4) budget cap, (5) data quality below threshold, (6) Strike 3. Processes may add domain-specific rows.
layers.name: Guard Rails
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — six canonical conditions are invariant from Bedrock. Domain additions are variable but don't change the table schema. Loaded before execution as halt triggers.

layers.format: Two sub-sections: (1) Numbered executable steps — action → expected result. (2) Three Primitives Check (Bedrock §1) — Thing existed? Flow reached? Change happened? Binary per question.
layers.name: Verification
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — format is fixed (numbered steps + three-question check). Specific test commands are variable fill. Run FIRST to validate before full pipeline execution. No verification = untestable = undeployable.

layers.format: Three sub-sections with structurally distinct schemas: (1) Process Metrics table (L22), (2) Sigma Tracking table (L23), (3) ORBT Gate Rules table (L24). Together they form the BUILD→OPERATE gate.
layers.name: Measurement
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — all three child layers (L22, L23, L24) are domesticated. The parent's remaining structure is the composition rule (all three required for state transitions) and the BUILD→OPERATE gate dependency — both locked by Bedrock §8. No further decomposition changes state machine logic.

layers.format: One schema: Per-step entry — 14 fields: trace_id, run_id, step, target, actual, delta, status, error_code, error_message, tools_used, duration_ms, cost_cents, timestamp, signed_by. Append-only.
layers.name: Execution Trace
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — 14 named fields with defined formats. Append-only constraint is locked. Individual entries are variable. A run summary is a derived view (CQRS: trace entries are writes, summary is a read aggregation) — not a separate schema.

layers.format: Birth Certificate — created ONLY after BUILD→OPERATE auditor sign-off. 7 fields: heir_ref, orbt_entered, orbt_exited, action, gates_passed (imo/ctb/circle), signed_by, signed_at. Append-only. No logbook during BUILD (Aviation Model, Bedrock §8).
layers.name: Certification Record (Logbook)
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — one entry schema with 7 fixed fields. Entries are variable fill. The 'no logbook during BUILD' rule is a constant from Bedrock §8.

layers.format: Two schemas: (1) Failure Pattern Registry — 7 columns: Pattern ID, Location, Error Code, First Seen, Occurrences, Strike Count, Status. (2) Strike Rules — 1→repair, 2→scrutiny, 3→Troubleshoot/Train→Airworthiness Directive (Bedrock §6/§8).
layers.name: Fleet Learning
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — registry schema + escalation rules locked by Bedrock §6/§8. Pattern content is variable fill.

layers.format: Table: 3 columns — Date, What Was Done, Knowledge Record ID. Append-only. Pointer to knowledge store for detail.
layers.name: Session History
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — three columns, append-only. Thinnest structural layer — a pointer to the knowledge store. Not parsed for execution, only for audit trail.

layers.format: Table: 5 columns — Element, ID, Format, Description, C-or-V. Runs C&V (Bedrock §2) on every data element. P(x;θ) evaluates each. Unidentified stored as unidentified, not discarded.
layers.name: Define Step (DMJ Step 1)
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — five-column table with fixed semantics. Elements themselves are variable fill. Cannot execute Map without this (forced dependency). DMJ Step 1.

layers.format: Table: 3 columns — Source, Target, Transform. Transform types: direct, classify, parse. Lookup table connecting Define output to target structure.
layers.name: Map Step (DMJ Step 2)
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — three-column table. Trivial once Define is complete. Cannot execute Join without this (forced dependency). DMJ Step 2.

layers.format: Table: 3 columns — Join Path, Type, Description. Join types: direct, indirect, fuzzy. Finds path to spine ID. Back-propagates to Define if gap found (the Circle, Bedrock §5).
layers.name: Join Step (DMJ Step 3)
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — three-column table. The Circle closes here — gap triggers return to L19 (Define). DMJ Step 3.

layers.format: Table: 5 columns — Metric, Unit, Baseline, Target, Tolerance. Defined BEFORE build starts. Each metric name is a constant (named, formatted). Values are variable fill.
layers.name: Process Metrics
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — five-column table. Metric definitions locked before build. Values fill in during runs.

layers.format: Table: 6 columns — Metric, Run 1, Run 2, Run 3+, Trend, Action. Trend values: TIGHTENING, FLAT, EXPANDING (Bedrock §2). Actions: none, investigate, reclassify. Requires 3+ runs before trends are valid.
layers.name: Sigma Tracking
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — three trend categories locked by Bedrock §2. Three action responses locked. Individual measurements across runs are variable fill.

layers.format: Table: 3 columns — From, To, Gate. Four transitions: (1) BUILD→OPERATE: 3 runs within tolerance + auditor sign-off. (2) OPERATE→REPAIR: any metric outside tolerance. (3) REPAIR→OPERATE: fix applied + metric within tolerance + auditor verification. (4) Any→TROUBLESHOOT/TRAIN: Strike 3 (Bedrock §6/§8).
layers.name: ORBT Gate Rules
layers.zoom_reason: STOP — four state transitions with fixed gate conditions. ORBT state machine locked by Bedrock §8. Gate conditions are constants. Current ORBT state is a variable.

reverse_route.target_value: a structured, executable, auditable process specification that any agent can parse and execute — domain-agnostic
